messages:
Morgan: Heads-up — need quick input on the fallback policy playback UX. Product wants a way to show the exact decision chain when a request falls back to a cheaper model. How much info should we surface in the console vs logs?
Priya: 👍 I think we should show an abbreviated chain in the console (3 most recent events) and link to full audit logs. Full logs can be heavy for product folks.
Samir: Agree. Also need to preserve token-level trace when we switch variants mid-generation. Otherwise playback/replay is meaningless.
Elaine: Token-level traces are expensive to retain. Could we store a summarized diff + pointers to KV cache snapshots instead of full tokens?
Javi: That could work. For playback UX we could show a timeline: trigger -> evaluation score -> action (route/fallback) -> result sample. Clicking an event would expand to the detailed log (audit store).
Morgan: Timeline sounds good. Question on triggers — should we show the raw metric (e.g., p95 latency 820ms) or a human-readable rule (latency > 700ms) that fired?
Priya: Both, if feasible. Show the rule name and the metric value that crossed the threshold. Example: "latency-breach (p95=820ms > 700ms)". Keeps it both actionable and auditable.
Samir: We also need to surface model compatibility checks that caused fallback: e.g., tokenizer mismatch, quantization incompatibility. Those are common for private deploys.
Elaine: Right — sometimes fallback happens because the chosen variant doesn't support streaming. UX should show "capability mismatch: streaming=false" not just "capacity".
Morgan: Nice. For audit retention, legal wants 90 days of full decision traces for enterprise. Can we mark the trace as "sensitive" so it gets different retention?
Javi: We already have per-customer retention flags in the audit store. We can attach metadata: {customer_id, retention_policy, redaction_level}. For the console, show a shield icon for sensitive traces and a redaction preview.
Samir: One more: simulate playback mode. Ops wants a sandbox where they can replay a historical request and see which fallback path would have been taken under current rules. Very helpful for rollout changes.
Priya: Ops sandbox=must-have. But watch out for side effects — replay must be read-only and not hit downstream caches/stores.
Elaine: Implementation note: replay should reconstruct inputs and run decision logic against stored runtime metrics snapshot, not re-run the full generation model. That keeps it safe.
Morgan: Good constraint. UX idea: toggle between "as-run" (what happened) and "as-configured" (what would've happened with current rules).
Javi: We'll need a diff view showing which rule changes flipped the action. Highlight rule name, old_eval, new_eval, and final action delta.
Samir: Telemetry: record one event per fallback with fields: request_id, trace_id, trigger_metric, model_from, model_to, decision_latency, snapshot_refs. Keep it compact for ingestion.
Priya: Also add a boolean field 'replay_safe' so ops knows whether a trace is eligible for sandbox replay.
Morgan: On the console, do we want to allow search by cause? e.g., "show fallbacks caused by tokenization errors".
Elaine: Yes — tag traces with reason codes. Maintain a canonical taxonomy: latency_breach, error_rate, capability_mismatch, quota_exceeded, model_error, tokenizer_error.
Javi: We'll map internal error strings to those codes at ingestion time. Makes queries performant.
Samir: UX micro-copy: when a user clicks a fallback event, show a short explanation + a link to a runbook. Example: "Routed to davinci-lite due to p95 latency breach. See runbook: [canary-fallback-guide]".
Priya: Don't forget RBAC: not everyone should see full traces. Provide role-based toggles: view-summary, view-full-audit. Console should hide expand button if user lacks permission.
Morgan: Good call. Also, product asked for a compact embeddable widget that teams can drop into their internal dashboards to show recent fallback health. Should be a small card: last 24h fallback rate, top triggers, recent examples.
Javi: Card can hit a summary endpoint we expose — pre-aggregated metrics. No PII in tile.
Elaine: One more edge case: oscillation. When the system keeps switching between variants rapidly, playback should compress repetitive handoffs and show a collapsed summary + option to expand.
Samir: Add a heuristic: collapse repeated identical actions within Xs into one line and show count. E.g., "fallback to model-x (repeated 6x in 12s)".
Priya: UX nit: use color + iconography: green for normal routing, orange for graceful degrade, red for hard-fallback. Keep accessible contrast.
Morgan: Nice. Ok action items: 1) Eng (Samir/Javi) to draft telemetry schema and minimal audit metadata for retention flags. 2) Product (Priya) to mock timeline UI and diff view. 3) Elaine to draft replay safety constraints and list of snapshot refs. 4) Morgan to coordinate RBAC scoping and runbook linking.
Samir: I'll put a PR for telemetry schema by EOD tomorrow.
Javi: I'll prototype timeline with expand/collapse states next sprint.
Priya: Will share Figma frames and microcopy by Friday.
Elaine: I'll write the replay safety doc and edge cases list.
deploy-bot: deployment started for branch "fallback-playback-schema" — build 1252
oncall-bot: oncall alert channel #eng-oncall added to the trace subscriptions for critical fallbacks
Morgan: Thanks all. If anyone has quick concerns about the retention or replay constraints speak up here; otherwise I'll sync with legal and shipping next week.
